For patients with limb-threatening ischemia and insufficient venous material, semi-closed endarterectomy of the superficial femoral artery combined with a short popliteo-crural bypass can be considered as an acceptable alternative to other treatments like primary angioplasty. This approach provides good outcomes for those who undergo it, although some limitations exist.

The benefits include improved or curing selected cases of type 1 diabetes during Roux-en-Y gastric bypass surgery. However, further studies are needed to confirm these results and determine the long-term effectiveness of this option.

In conclusion, semi-closed endarterectomy combined with a short popliteo-crural bypass might be an alternative for limb-threatening ischemia in specific cases but should be carefully evaluated on a case-by-case basis. Patients who choose this treatment should be aware of its limitations and potential risks.
